title: Business Idioms 2
completion_message: ¡Fantástico! Expresiones como 'red tape' o 'read between the lines' le darán a tu inglés ese toque auténtico que impresiona a colegas y clientes internacionales.

parts.visual:
Burocracia y Comprensión: 
- Red tape (Exceso de burocracia / Papeleo). 
Ej: To get the permit, we have to deal with a lot of red tape. 
- Read between the lines (Leer entre líneas / Entender lo que no se dice directamente). 
Ej: He said the project is 'fine', but reading between the lines, I think it's failing.
parts.audio: Bureaucracy and Understanding. 'Red tape' means excessive bureaucracy or paperwork. For example: To get the permit, we have to deal with a lot of red tape. 'Read between the lines' means to understand a hidden or implied meaning. For example: He said the project is 'fine', but reading between the lines, I think it's failing.

parts.visual:
Trabajo y Despido: 
- Get the sack / Be given the sack (Ser despedido). 
Ej: He was caught stealing and got the sack. 
- Learn the ropes (Aprender cómo se hace un trabajo / Las cuerdas). 
Ej: It will take her a few weeks to learn the ropes.
parts.audio: Work and Firing. 'Get the sack' or 'Be given the sack' is an informal way to say 'to be fired'. For example: He was caught stealing and got the sack. 'Learn the ropes' means to learn the basics of a job or task. For example: It will take her a few weeks to learn the ropes.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el modismo avanzado correcto para la situación.

questions.question: Setting up a business in this country involves too much ____ tape. (Burocracia / Papeleo excesivo).
questions.explanation: Red tape = excesiva burocracia, normas oficiales excesivas.

questions.question: The email was polite, but reading between the ____, they are very angry. (Leer entre líneas).
questions.explanation: Read between the lines = deducir un significado oculto.

questions.question: If you keep coming to work late, you are going to get the ____. (Ser despedido).
questions.explanation: Get the sack = ser despedido (informal pero muy usado en negocios, similar a 'get the boot').

questions.question: Don't worry if you make mistakes at first. You are still learning the ____. (Aprender las nociones básicas de un trabajo).
questions.explanation: Learn the ropes = aprender cómo funcionan las cosas en un nuevo trabajo.

questions.question: We are currently in the ____, but we hope to make a profit next year. (En números rojos / Perdiendo dinero).
questions.explanation: In the red = perdiendo dinero, tener deudas.

questions.question: Finally, our startup is in the ____! We made a $10,000 profit. (En números negros / Con ganancias).
questions.explanation: In the black = siendo rentable, ganando dinero.

questions.question: This project is a piece of ____. We can finish it in an hour. (Pan comido / Muy fácil).
questions.explanation: A piece of cake = algo extremadamente fácil.

questions.question: The manager passed the ____ and blamed his team for the failure. (Pasar la pelota / Evadir la responsabilidad).
questions.explanation: Pass the buck = pasarle la responsabilidad o la culpa a otro.

questions.question: I don't agree entirely, but I'll play devil's ____ to see the other side of the argument. (Abogado del diablo).
questions.explanation: Play devil's advocate = defender la posición contraria solo por debatir o explorar opciones.

questions.question: By signing the contract without reading it, you really shot yourself in the ____. (Darse un tiro en el pie / Perjudicarse a sí mismo).
questions.explanation: Shoot oneself in the foot = hacer algo que termina perjudicándote a ti mismo.

questions.question: Let's start with a blank ____ and design the product from zero. (Borrón y cuenta nueva / Pizarra limpia).
questions.explanation: A blank slate / A clean slate = un nuevo comienzo sin verse afectado por el pasado.

questions.question: The CEO's resignation came out of the ____. Nobody expected it. (De la nada / Totalmente inesperado).
questions.explanation: Out of the blue = inesperadamente, por sorpresa.

questions.question: To stay ahead of the ____, we must invest heavily in R&D. (Llevar la delantera / Estar a la vanguardia).
questions.explanation: Ahead of the curve = ser innovador, adelantarse a las tendencias.

questions.question: The new employee is trying to bite off more than he can ____. (Abarcar más de lo que puede apretar/masticar).
questions.explanation: Bite off more than you can chew = intentar asumir más responsabilidades de las que uno puede manejar.

questions.question: By combining both software companies, we get the best of both ____. (Lo mejor de ambos mundos).
questions.explanation: The best of both worlds = una situación donde disfrutas de dos ventajas diferentes a la vez.

questions.question: Our competitor went bankrupt. We need to strike while the ____ is hot! (Golpear mientras el hierro está caliente / Aprovechar la oportunidad).
questions.explanation: Strike while the iron is hot = aprovechar la oportunidad en el momento exacto.

questions.question: The presentation was going badly until Sarah saved the ____ with her brilliant idea. (Salvar el día/la situación).
questions.explanation: Save the day = rescatar una situación que iba mal.

questions.question: The marketing strategy went down in ____. It was a total disaster. (Fracasar estrepitosamente / Caer en llamas).
questions.explanation: Go down in flames = fallar espectacular o catastróficamente.

questions.question: He's an unreliable partner. He will drop you like a hot ____ if he finds a better deal. (Papa caliente / Abandonar rápidamente).
questions.explanation: Drop someone/something like a hot potato = deshacerse de alguien o algo rápidamente porque es problemático.

questions.question: Our back is against the ____. We have to sign this deal or we go bankrupt. (Entre la espada y la pared / De espaldas contra la pared).
questions.explanation: Back against the wall = estar en una situación desesperada sin muchas opciones.
